Sample review: My-PIT Sign and General Decimal Arithmetic test data

Verdicts
- d5e4db7daf438660a0659b8eb31f5c4c2fb7c47f56440aef79d30bd1c78cf328: BENIGN
  My-PIT Sign 2.0, an Inno Setup 5.5.7 Unicode installer for a Vietnamese
  invoice/tax-document XML signer (myinvoiceSign.exe / EInvoiceTools).
- f07a006c8deb5efdd03bc2626128503498d35238791c32b42542834568665a00: BENIGN
  IBM General Decimal Arithmetic 2.59 coefficient-shift conformance tests.
- f076d3a2f7935563db48a25173c16f08ed51e4a06cf23778b1e76c815b0c74a1: BENIGN
  IBM General Decimal Arithmetic 2.59 decDouble coefficient-rotate tests.

Reverse engineering
Ran atomscan and cleave facts on all three full sample paths before changes.
Facts include extracted ASCII/UTF-16 data; no decoded content was assumed to be
executable merely because it resembled an API, address or encoding.

Extracted every Inno member using innoextract. Independently parsed the loader
header, verified metadata block/chunk CRC32 values and decompressed the LZMA
setup metadata. Disassembled the complete 761-byte IFPS script with Binary
Refinery. InitializeSetup invokes ShellExec twice with wmic.exe and process
where name-like predicates for myinvoiceSign and MsInvoice, followed by delete.
This stops previous signer processes before replacing files. It returns true.
The other script procedure is empty. No download, arbitrary execution channel
or security-product termination is present in that script. FileExists is used
in declarative shortcut/run-entry conditions. The package installs the signer,
icons, ordinary libraries and PDB/XML documentation; it creates desktop and
common-startup shortcuts and launches the installed signer.

Disassembled all managed method bodies in myinvoiceSign.exe using dnfile/dncil,
resolving method, field and user-string tokens, branches and exception regions.
Entry token 0600003e runs TrayApplicationContext, whose constructor registers
SignHost. Config overrides the default localhost:24039 with 127.0.0.1:24038.
Startup installs Web API attribute routes and CORS. SignController exposes
Version, TestConn and XmlCertificated; the latter enters ExecuteCertificatedData
and a modal certificate selector. Cancellation returns an error. Selected
certificate data flows to the signing form. GetListCert reads CurrentUser/My.
The certificate Export call receives enum value 1 (public Cert), not PFX.
ExecSignData constructs SignedXml, sets its signing key, references the invoice
node and signing-time object, computes the signature and inserts signature XML.
Request-specific download/sign/upload paths transfer invoice and tax-document
XML and public certificate metadata through RestSharp/HttpClient. No private-key
export or unrelated credential harvesting was found. Registry URI-association
helpers are defined, but Main's InitializeService is empty and does not call
them. No loader/eval, shell payload, hidden C2 task dispatcher or obfuscation
was found in the application.

An accurate security concern remains: all nine RestSharp certificate-validation
lambdas (RVA 8b6f..8b87) are ldc.i4.1; ret, and their callers install those
callbacks before HTTP operations. This disables server authentication. The
existing notable callback-assignment observation is retained; a setter string
alone cannot distinguish these bodies from a legitimate pinning callback, so
no unsupported bypass signature or hostile verdict was manufactured.

Fetched the effective configured server at https://chungtu.mypit.vn/ and its
main.js. It serves an MS INVOICE Angular application; the configured API root
/tax/rest/s1 returned HTTP 404 without a specific route. The old hardcoded
hoadon.webbit.vn default did not resolve. Current availability is not proof of
historical server behavior. The local call graph, user certificate selection
and document signing/upload data flow establish the program's purpose.

Bundled RestSharp 106.1.0 net452, Swashbuckle.Core 5.6.0 net40 and Owin 1.0.0
net40 DLLs are byte-identical to official api.nuget.org flat-container packages.
Other bundled Microsoft/Newtonsoft/BouncyCastle components have verified intact
Authenticode signatures in the analysis; signing is corroboration, not a
blanket behavioral exception. Swagger/jQuery browser assets explain XMLHTTP,
DOM, upload and editor references inside Swashbuckle.Core.dll.

Read every noncomment decimal-data line. The only directives set version,
precision, rounding and numeric context; each remaining line supplies a named
shift/rotate operation, numeric operands and expected result/status. There are
no includes, execution directives, executable dependencies or hidden bytes.
Fetched https://speleotrove.com/decimal/dectest.zip from the successor of the
referenced IBM site. Test bodies match upstream 2.62 exactly; differences are
copyright/contact/URL headers and the 2.59-to-2.62 version declaration.
The format specification is https://speleotrove.com/decimal/dectest.html.

Why the hostile source labels may be wrong
The EXE's generic dropper/riskware labels are consistent with heuristics on an
unsigned compressed installer, hidden WMIC launches, startup installation and
cryptographic/private-key API references. This is an explanation of plausible
false-positive causes, not attribution to any vendor's internal detection.
The actual operations fit installation and interactive invoice signing.
The decimal files contain only upstream arithmetic test data. A source could
have inherited an enclosing collection/package label or misclassified numeric
fixture content; no specific source rationale was supplied for these files.

Trait changes and placement audit
Added a documentation-reference observation and a counted expected-result-row
observation; their conjunction identifies the General Decimal Arithmetic
conformance corpus without relying on filenames, hashes or exact test values.
The new corpus identity never suppresses executable behavior.

Moved embedded XMLHTTP construction from process/script/wsh to HTTP client
XMLHTTP, Ace editor access from SQL to UI input, and CLR member lookup/delegate
references plus their resolver composites to metaprogramming/reflection.
Descriptions distinguish API-name references from proven calls.

Auditing the full reflection population before admitting those moves found
method generation and property writes in that directory. Moved Ruby method
definition/alias operations to metaprogramming/generation and Ruby constant /
Python builtin assignments to data/property/assign. The alias-method rule's
unsupported generic T1059 mapping was removed separately. No matcher, effective
platform/type scope, criticality or exclusion changed in these moves.
The reflection leaf now has 99 rules; no new partition or budget was created.
All exact consumers were rewritten. The old directory selector data/db/sql in
the classic ASP file-manager rule intentionally no longer accepts an editor
control as database evidence. Other reviewed selectors do not require added
members. id-map.json records all moved IDs. Existing loader rules left in the
source directories retain their meanings and are outside this migration.

Verification
13 positive/near-miss fixtures pass (cases.json and results.json). The Python
execution-builtin fixture retains test-directory suppression; the same source
outside test directories matches the moved rule. Tests include two reflected
API observations versus one, HTTP versus non-HTTP COM, editor versus ordinary
input, full decimal corpus versus documentation only / rows only / two rows.
After rescanning the installer, all findings and severities are identical after
applying the intentional ID map, including its archive members. It has zero
suspicious or hostile findings. Re-ran atomscan on all three original samples;
both decimal files now carry documentation and operation-row observations.
Final make validate is run after marker creation as required.
